quests.explanation: 'I've never been to' is the standard way to say you haven't visited a place.
quests.textToSpeak: I've never been to Singapore before.
quests.correctAnswer: I've never been to Singapore before.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Singapore' /ˈsɪŋəpɔː/ has /ŋ/ without a hard 'g' sound. 'I've never' /aɪv ˈnevə/ is a quick pair.

quests.explanation: 'Have lived' plus 'for' and a period shows a situation that started in the past and continues.
quests.textToSpeak: We've lived here for about three years.
quests.correctAnswer: We've lived here for about three years.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Lived' /lɪvd/ ends in /vd/. 'About' /əˈbaʊt/ is stressed on BOUT. 'Three' starts with /θ/.

quests.explanation: 'Yet' in a question with 'have' asks whether something is done by now.
quests.textToSpeak: Have you finished the report yet?
quests.correctAnswer: Have you finished the report yet?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Have you' sounds like 'həv-ya'. 'Report' /rɪˈpɔːt/ is stressed on PORT. 'Finished' /ˈfɪnɪʃt/ ends in /ʃt/.

quests.hint: Stress falls on the third syllable: rez-er-VAY-shun.
quests.explanation: 'A reservation under the name…' is what you say at hotel check-in.
quests.textToSpeak: I have a reservation under the name Carter.
quests.correctAnswer: I have a reservation under the name Carter.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Reservation' /ˌrezəˈveɪʃn/ has main stress on VAY. 'Under' /ˈʌndə/ is stressed on UN.

quests.explanation: Asking what's included is a key travel question, and 'included' works like an adjective here.
quests.textToSpeak: Is the Wi-Fi included in the price?
quests.correctAnswer: Is the Wi-Fi included in the price?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Included' /ɪnˈkluːdɪd/ ends with a full extra syllable. 'Wi-Fi' /ˈwaɪfaɪ/ has the same vowel twice.

quests.hint: Say 'checkout' as one word with stress on CHECK.
quests.explanation: 'Could we get' is a softer way to ask than 'can we have'.
quests.textToSpeak: Could we get a late checkout tomorrow?
quests.correctAnswer: Could we get a late checkout tomorrow?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Checkout' as a noun is stressed on the first part: CHECK-out. 'Tomorrow' /təˈmɒrəʊ/ is stressed on MOR.

quests.explanation: 'Since' plus a starting point works with present perfect for ongoing symptoms.
quests.textToSpeak: I've had a headache since this morning.
quests.correctAnswer: I've had a headache since this morning.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Headache' /ˈhedeɪk/ is stressed on HEAD. 'Since' /sɪns/ ends in /ns/. 'Morning' /ˈmɔːnɪŋ/ has a long vowel.

quests.explanation: 'Anything for' plus a problem is the natural way to ask a pharmacist for a remedy.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you have anything for a sore throat?
quests.correctAnswer: Do you have anything for a sore throat?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Anything' /ˈeniθɪŋ/ has /θ/ in the middle. 'Throat' /θrəʊt/ starts with /θr/ and glides on the vowel.

quests.hint: Stress 'one' and 'every' so the dosage is clear.
quests.explanation: Medicine instructions follow 'take + amount + when'. Clear pronunciation of 'one tablet' matters here.
quests.textToSpeak: You should take one tablet after every meal.
quests.correctAnswer: You should take one tablet after every meal.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Tablet' /ˈtæblət/ is stressed on TAB. 'Every' is usually said as two syllables, /ˈevri/. 'Meal' has a long /iː/.

quests.hint: Stress 'soup' and 'salad' to keep the two orders apart.
quests.explanation: 'I'll have…' is how you order for yourself, and 'wants' describes another person's choice.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll have the soup, and my friend wants the salad.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll have the soup, and my friend wants the salad.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Soup' /suːp/ has a long vowel. 'Salad' /ˈsæləd/ is stressed on SAL. 'Wants' /wɒnts/ ends in /nts/.

quests.hint: 'Dessert' has a buzzing /z/ in the middle.
quests.explanation: Asking for a specific menu is a common polite request in restaurants.
quests.textToSpeak: Could we see the dessert menu, please?
quests.correctAnswer: Could we see the dessert menu, please?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Dessert' /dɪˈzɜːt/ is stressed on SERT. 'Menu' /ˈmenjuː/ is stressed on MEN.

quests.hint: Stress 'without' so the correction is clear.
quests.explanation: A polite correction opens with 'Excuse me', and 'without' names exactly what's missing.
quests.textToSpeak: Excuse me, we ordered this dish without onions.
quests.correctAnswer: Excuse me, we ordered this dish without onions.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Ordered' /ˈɔːdəd/ has two syllables. 'Onions' /ˈʌnjənz/ starts with /ʌ/ and ends in /nz/.

quests.explanation: 'Keep + -ing' describes a repeated problem. It's the natural way to report a fault.
quests.textToSpeak: My screen keeps freezing every few minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: My screen keeps freezing every few minutes.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Freezing' /ˈfriːzɪŋ/ has a long /iː/ and a /z/. 'Keeps' ends in /ps/.

quests.hint: Give 'can't' a strong vowel so it isn't heard as 'can'.
quests.explanation: 'So' links the problem and its result. 'Log in' is a phrasal verb.
quests.textToSpeak: I forgot my password, so I can't log in.
quests.correctAnswer: I forgot my password, so I can't log in.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Password' /ˈpɑːswɜːd/ is stressed on PASS. 'Can't' /kænt/ has a strong vowel, and 'log in' is two clear beats.

quests.explanation: 'The file you sent' is a natural short relative clause, with no 'that' needed.
quests.textToSpeak: The file you sent won't open on my phone.
quests.correctAnswer: The file you sent won't open on my phone.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Won't' /wəʊnt/ glides and ends in /nt/. 'Sent' /sent/ ends in /nt/ too. Stress 'file', 'sent' and 'open'.

quests.explanation: 'I'd like to' plus a verb is the polite way to state a need at a counter.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to open a savings account.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to open a savings account.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Savings' /ˈseɪvɪŋz/ ends in /ŋz/. 'Account' /əˈkaʊnt/ is stressed on COUNT.

quests.explanation: Questions joined by 'or' offer a choice. The rise-then-fall shows the list is complete.
quests.textToSpeak: Can I pay by card or do I need cash?
quests.correctAnswer: Can I pay by card or do I need cash?
quests.pronunciationTips: The pitch goes up on 'card' and down on 'cash'. 'Cash' /kæʃ/ ends in /ʃ/.

quests.explanation: 'Should have' plus a past participle says something was expected but hasn't happened.
quests.textToSpeak: The parcel should have arrived by now.
quests.correctAnswer: The parcel should have arrived by now.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Should have' /ˈʃʊdəv/. 'Parcel' /ˈpɑːsl/ has two syllables. 'Arrived' /əˈraɪvd/ is stressed on RIVED.

quests.explanation: 'Half past ten' means 10:30 in spoken English.
quests.textToSpeak: We have a team meeting at half past ten.
quests.correctAnswer: We have a team meeting at half past ten.
quests.pronunciationTips: In British English, 'half' /hɑːf/ and 'past' /pɑːst/ use a long vowel. 'Meeting' /ˈmiːtɪŋ/ is stressed on MEET.

quests.explanation: 'Catch' here means 'hear clearly'. It's a polite way to ask someone to repeat.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, I didn't catch your name.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Catch' /kætʃ/ ends in /tʃ/. The /t/ in 'didn't' is very light before /k/. 'Your' is weak.

quests.hint: Stress 'working' and 'not finished' to contrast progress with completion.
quests.explanation: Present continuous shows ongoing work. 'Not finished' states the current status.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm working on the budget, but I'm not finished.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm working on the budget, but I'm not finished.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Budget' /ˈbʌdʒɪt/ has /dʒ/ in the middle. 'Finished' /ˈfɪnɪʃt/ ends in /ʃt/.

quests.hint: 'A few times a week' runs together as one chunk.
quests.explanation: 'A few times a week' answers 'how often'. 'Try to' plus a verb states an effort.
quests.textToSpeak: I try to run a few times a week.
quests.correctAnswer: I try to run a few times a week.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Times a week' flows like 'time-zə-week'. 'Try to' becomes 'try-tə'.

quests.explanation: Ending with 'than I do' avoids repeating 'play the guitar'.
quests.textToSpeak: She plays the guitar much better than I do.
quests.correctAnswer: She plays the guitar much better than I do.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Guitar' /ɡɪˈtɑː/ is stressed on TAR. 'Better' /ˈbetə/ carries the comparison, and the final 'do' takes the last stress.

quests.explanation: 'Thinking of' plus -ing describes a plan you haven't fixed yet.
quests.textToSpeak: We're thinking of joining a yoga class next month.
quests.correctAnswer: We're thinking of joining a yoga class next month.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Thinking' /ˈθɪŋkɪŋ/. 'Yoga' /ˈjəʊɡə/ is stressed on YO. 'Joining' has the /ɔɪ/ diphthong.

quests.hint: Stress 'stopped working' as the key problem.
quests.explanation: 'Stopped working' is the everyday way to report that a machine has failed.
quests.textToSpeak: The heating stopped working last night, and it's freezing.
quests.correctAnswer: The heating stopped working last night, and it's freezing.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Stopped' /stɒpt/ ends in /pt/ with no extra vowel. 'Heating' /ˈhiːtɪŋ/ has a long /iː/.

quests.explanation: 'Was supposed to' states an expectation that wasn't met.
quests.textToSpeak: The delivery was supposed to come this morning.
quests.correctAnswer: The delivery was supposed to come this morning.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Supposed to' is /səˈpəʊstə/, with the /d/ dropped. 'Delivery' /dɪˈlɪvəri/ is stressed on LIV.

quests.hint: Join 'come and look' into one flow.
quests.explanation: 'Could someone' makes a polite, impersonal repair request.
quests.textToSpeak: Could someone come and look at the sink tomorrow?
quests.correctAnswer: Could someone come and look at the sink tomorrow?
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Sink' /sɪŋk/ ends in /ŋk/. 'Tomorrow' /təˈmɒrəʊ/ is stressed on MOR. 'Come and' becomes 'com-ən'.

quests.explanation: Present perfect continuous stresses how long something has lasted, which is useful for complaints.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been waiting for twenty minutes, and nobody's helped me.
quests.correctAnswer: I've been waiting for twenty minutes, and nobody's helped me.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'I've been' is quick, /aɪv biːn/. 'Nobody's' /ˈnəʊbədiz/ contracts 'nobody has'. 'Helped' /helpt/ ends in /lpt/.

quests.explanation: 'If you're free' is a friendly opening, and 'could' makes the suggestion soft.
quests.textToSpeak: If you're free on Saturday, we could go hiking.
quests.correctAnswer: If you're free on Saturday, we could go hiking.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Saturday' /ˈsætədeɪ/ is stressed on SAT. 'Hiking' /ˈhaɪkɪŋ/ has the diphthong /aɪ/.

quests.hint: 'Whether' starts with /w/ and has a voiced /ð/.
quests.explanation: 'Whether to' plus a verb expresses a choice you haven't made yet.
quests.textToSpeak: I wasn't sure whether to call or send a text.
quests.correctAnswer: I wasn't sure whether to call or send a text.
quests.pronunciationTips: 'Whether' /ˈweðə/. 'Wasn't' /ˈwɒznt/ has two syllables. 'Text' /tekst/ ends in /kst/.
